packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-15: UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Exposure and process statement
- No identification or reading of the work reached me from outside the images. The only identifying text I saw is a modern pencil shelfmark on the parchment: "Stams, STA, Frg. 113r" (image-005/006, face A) and "Stams, STA, Frg. 113v" (image-012/017, face B). I did not identify the work or author.
- Process note: I viewed all 22 images, some of them twice. Image content was later dropped from my working context ("media removed"), so near the end I re-opened images 001, 012 and 017 to confirm that the transcription below matches the leaf, and it does. Nothing else was opened (packet.json was not read). This is a blind first reading.
- 017:2 is better read as "ut p(er)? duas res" (the abbreviation is uncertain).

Conventions
- Lines are text lines (staves not counted), numbered from the top of the named tile. Tiles overlap; repeated lines are cited once.
- [red] ... = rubric ink, [black] = return to text ink. Expansions in (); "?" = uncertain reading; [illegible] = could not read; [gap] = space left in a text line under a melisma (not a loss).

==================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observation only)
==================================================================
Each face is a horizontal strip: two leaf-halves separated by a central fold (brown stain, sewing slits), so an opened bifolium or two conjoint halves, trimmed above and below. Each half has two columns, so there are four columns per face. Gothic textualis in brown ink with red rubrics, red and black flourished initials, red four-line staves, black square/Gothic-type neumes, letter clefs (c, f) at the start of each staff. No running titles, glosses or marginalia except the pencil shelfmark. Losses: torn top edge with modern paper repairs, holes at the fold, abrasion, water stains. The foot of each column is trimmed.

Face A ("113r"; overview 001; tiles 002-011)
- Col 1: fully notated chant with red cues ("In lau.", "anty", "ps", "a").
- Col 2: rubrical directions, several lines written wholly in red, then notated chants.
- Col 3: continuous prose with red Hebrew-letter rubrics (Ioth, Caph, Lamech, Men, Num, Samech, Ayn).
- Col 4: same prose (Res, Sen, Tau), then red "Responsorium" and notated chant with red initial S.
Face B ("113v"; overview 012; tiles 013-022)
- Col 1: prose with Hebrew-letter rubrics (Deleth to Num).
- Col 2: prose (Coph, Res, Sen, Tau), then a notated piece with red R and red I, and a red V.
- Col 3: notated piece with red I and V, then a large red C opening prose, with a short inserted staff at the right.
- Col 4: prose, then red R and red C opening notated chant.
Tentative interpretation (not identification): a noted office book, with lessons marked by Hebrew letters and followed by responsories, and rubrics giving performance directions.

Selection: I read all four columns on both faces as far as the leaf allows. Weak spots are listed under Limitations.
